source.unit: De architectura IX.3.1–3, entire chapter including transition to the next topic.
source.checked: Complete institutional English translation chapter read; translation/witness distinctions remain.
source.content: The annual account links zodiac progress to day-length change, equinoxes and solstices. It also equates courses at separated positions, while retaining named stellar landmarks and eighth-part conventions.

design.whole_passage_relation: Full target candidate must express both annual halves, extrema, explicit equal-course pairings, stellar landmarks and transition. It is not a twelve-name substitution or month-order ranking.
two_reused_input_cases: The text equates the solar course at separated positions; equal day length would be a further interpreted consequence, not a supplied numerical equality.
The same day-length quantity increases on one branch and decreases on another; equality does not equate the events.
design.rival: A static zodiac enumeration, or one monotonic annual scale in which later always means longer.
design.distinct_consequence: A fixed EQUAL relation links separate states, while INCREASE/DECREASE are directional and retain branch context. Same value does not imply same phase identity.
design.falsifier: Fail if complete repeated-value binding collapses equal-course positions into one sign, or one change operator must reverse sign without a written branch/condition.
design.smallest_step: Predeclare the complete source comparison graph and all source names before target authoring; retain all stated eighth-part/landmark details and test two paired-state consequences.
new_costs: No inferred modern astronomical numerical precision, latitude or month lengths.
No rotation of target blocks to maximize match; no fixed Latin spelling cipher.
Keep course equality distinct from measured day-length equality; the latter requires an explicit bridge.
predecessors: RAW495/498/503 concerned IX.8.9 clock mechanics and month holes, not IX.3 solar causation; no clock vocabulary inherited.
